title: A Facilitator Action Precedent's Label must always be created as 'Aligned', with misalignment findings coming only later
content:
A.1.2.2.2.14 gives Facilitator Action Precedent Documents a Label component indicating "whether the Facilitator's action is considered aligned or misaligned according to the principles and rules of governance," and then fixes its initial value: "The Label must always be marked as Aligned when it is created by the Facilitator, and further action by Sky Governance can directly modify this later according to the specifications of the Atlas Documents relevant to appealing Facilitator Actions."

This is an act-first, review-later architecture with the default set to approval. A facilitator does not seek clearance and does not record doubt — they act, self-label as aligned, and the record stands unless governance overturns it. If the label is later flipped to misaligned, it "must also specify the penalty that is applied to the Facilitator for misalignment," so the same field carries both the verdict and the sanction.

The reasoning is operational: facilitators must be able to move at the speed of events, and a pre-approval requirement would make every action wait on a governance cycle. The cost is that the burden of challenge falls entirely on governance — nothing surfaces automatically as questionable, and an action's record is presumptively favourable to the actor who wrote it.

What makes it workable is the surrounding forcing function: A.1.2.2.2.14 says the creation of a Facilitator Action Precedent "is the formal method that Facilitators use to record Atlas Interpretations, take action against misalignment, or explicitly approve ecosystem activity." There is no unrecorded facilitator action. Governance trades pre-approval for a guaranteed, uniform audit trail — and takes on the duty of reading it.
description: A.1.2.2.2.14 makes facilitators self-certify their own actions as aligned; only subsequent Sky Governance action can flip the label to misaligned and attach a penalty.
